description: §19.10.4 — the exits that fire NONE of the §19.10.4 codes. Unchanged since S450: a `break` / `continue` whose loop is INSIDE the `transaction { }`, a `fail` (§19.10.3 ROLLBACK) nested in an `if`, and a `return` AFTER the block. ⚑ ADDED AT S453 (B1a, ruled): a `return` out of the block (`early`), and a `break` (`leaveLoop`) / `continue` (`skipPass`) whose loop is OUTSIDE it — all three were the S450 interim E-TRANSACTION-CONTROL-FLOW refusal and are now legal, rolling the block back and letting the exit proceed. `early` and `leaveLoop` are the two sites the old ../transaction-control-flow-neg/ case asserted as errors; they are moved here verbatim, so this file and that one together record the direction of the ruling. The ROLLBACK itself is proved by execution in ../../server-db/sql-transaction-exit-rollback-rt/ — a codes-only case cannot see it.
rationale: §19.10.3 (S453): "A `return`, or a `break` / `continue` whose target is outside the block, SHALL roll the transaction back before the exit proceeds; only normal completion COMMITs." A loop's own `break` / `continue` never leaves the block; a `return` after the block runs once the block has committed. Provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S449 (B1a).
